entities.summary: Gaston-Pierre-Charles de Lévis-Lomagne, duc de Mirepoix, maréchal de France (1757) and Ambassador of Louis XV, was a French aristocrat. He was born on December 2, 1699, in Belleville, France, and died on September 24, 1757. Lévis-Lomagne's significance lies in his role as a military leader and diplomat during the reign of Louis XV, who oversaw significant military campaigns and territorial expansion. The French and Austrian Wars, which lasted from 1740 to 1748, were a major part of Lévis-Lomagne's career, showcasing his strategic prowess and diplomacy. His involvement in these conflicts led to the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle in 1748, which ended the war and secured French territorial gains. Lévis-Lomagne's legacy is also tied to his service as Ambassador to the Holy Roman Empire, where he played a crucial role in negotiating the Treaty of Vienna in 1738. This treaty marked a significant shift in the balance of power in Europe, with France emerging as a dominant force. His influence extended beyond politics, as he was a patron of the arts and a supporter of various cultural institutions. The Palace of Versailles, where Lévis-Lomagne often resided, was a hub for artistic and cultural expression during his time. This connection to the arts highlights Lévis-Lomagne's role as a patron and supporter of various creative endeavors. Despite his influential role, Lévis-Lomagne's life was also marked by personal struggles, including his involvement in several scandals and controversies. His marriage to Marie-Thérèse de Lévis-Lomagne, who was a member of the French nobility, added to the intrigue surrounding his personal life. The couple had several children together, including a son who went on to become a notable military leader in his own right. Lévis-Lomagne's impact on French history is undeniable, and his legacy continues to be studied by historians and scholars today. The significance of his life and career lies in the lasting impact he had on French politics, diplomacy, and culture, shaping the trajectory of the country's development during the 18th century.
